title: Cashew Cheese
subtitle: a sliceable, dairy-free “cheese”
menu_blurb: A creamy, sliceable cashew “cheese” set with agar, ready for pizza, eggplant parmesan, arancini, or a simple sandwich.
intro: A great alternative to cheese. Truthfully, I wouldn’t call it “cheese,” but it has a great taste and can replace cheese in many recipes.
origin: Cashew cheese grew out of the raw food and vegan movements as a dairy-free alternative and became widely available in the early 21st century. Nut-based cheeses made from almonds date back to at least the 15th century, but using cashews is a relatively modern idea.

mise_en_place.label: Soak
mise_en_place.task: Cashews in hot water for about 30 minutes

mise_en_place.label: Tools
mise_en_place.task: A small pot for the agar mixture, a blender, and a cup or container to set the cheese in

steps.title: Prepare
instructions: Soak the cashews in just-boiled water for 30 minutes.
Measure out the spices for the cheese and the ingredients for the agar mixture.
Spray the inside of the cup or container with cooking spray.

steps.title: Blend
instructions: Blend them with the rest of the cheese ingredients until thick and smooth.

steps.title: Cook the agar
instructions: Add the water and agar powder to a small saucepan and bring to a boil. Lower the heat and stir constantly until thickened, about 1 minute.
Add the blended cashew mixture and stir for another minute, until thick and combined.

steps.title: Set overnight
instructions: Pour into the greased cup and cover.
Let it set overnight before using.
Turn the cup upside down onto parchment paper to release it. For storage, wrap it in foil and a plastic bag.

steps.title: Use it
instructions: Add it to whatever you are making, like pizza, eggplant parmesan, [arancini](recipe.html?r=arancini), or a simple sandwich.

tips.label: Flavor boost
tips.tip: For a more herby taste, add basil and oregano. For more color, add turmeric.

tips.label: Substitution
tips.tip: Swap the avocado oil for coconut oil.

tips.label: Meal prep hack
tips.tip: Keeps well in the fridge for 5 days or more, or in the freezer for a long time.

facts: 6 to 9 g fat, mostly heart-healthy monounsaturated
nutrition.notes: Significantly lower in saturated fat than dairy cheese.

notebook.question: Is cashew cheese good for you?
answer: Homemade cashew cheese is a nutrient-dense alternative to dairy, typically higher in fiber and healthy fats but lower in protein and calcium.

notebook.question: What’s the difference between cashew cheese and mozzarella?
answer: They differ in nutrition, ingredients, and how they behave in cooking. Here is how they compare, per 1 oz (28 g).

table.label: Cholesterol
table.text: Cashew cheese: 0 mg · Mozzarella: about 15 to 20 mg

table.label: Saturated fat
table.text: Cashew cheese: about 1 to 2 g · Mozzarella: about 3.5 to 5 g

table.label: Protein
table.text: Cashew cheese: about 2 to 4 g · Mozzarella: about 6 to 7 g

table.label: Calcium
table.text: Cashew cheese: low unless fortified · Mozzarella: high (about 15 to 20% DV)

table.label: Fiber
table.text: Cashew cheese: about 1 to 2 g · Mozzarella: 0 g

table.label: Digestibility
table.text: Cashew cheese is lactose-free · Mozzarella contains lactose

benefits.label: Fat quality
benefits.text: Cashew cheese contains mostly heart-healthy unsaturated fats from nuts, while dairy mozzarella is higher in saturated fat, which can raise LDL cholesterol.

benefits.label: Ingredients
benefits.text: Cashew cheese is made from whole cashews, water, nutritional yeast, and lemon juice or cultures. Mozzarella is made from cow or buffalo milk, salt, and rennet.

benefits.label: Melt and stretch
benefits.text: Mozzarella is prized for how it melts and stretches. Some cashew versions use tapioca starch or agar to mimic this, but they rarely match it exactly.

benefits.label: Micronutrients
benefits.text: Cashew cheese is a good source of magnesium and manganese, but lacks the vitamins A and D found in or added to dairy.

benefits.label: Environmental impact
benefits.text: Cashew cheese uses significantly less land and water than dairy production.
